title: A refit cuts the timing difference of two TOI-682 models from 3.07 to 0.93 minutes in twelve simulated transits
abstract: A new three-planet fit cuts its root mean square timing difference from a two-planet example from 3.068 to 0.930 minutes across twelve simulated future transits, while retaining a past timing-plus-shape chi-square of 21.156. Its extra planet mass changes from 28.43 to 60.95 Earth masses. The fit reaches an iteration limit, and we do not test its stability or fit individual RVs. We test whether twelve future transit times can separate two published TOI-682 models: a two-planet example near 16 days and a three-planet example with an extra planet near 27 days. At one-minute timing precision, the fixed-orbit squared separation is 112.96 for a greedy selected set. Allowing local orbit changes reduces the weaker separation score to 12.50. Twelve regular visits give 2.99. We also refit both neighborhoods to the real past measurements plus noise-free future times from each model. We preserve all final fit endpoints and losses. Thus fixed forecast lines can overstate the test of these models. This is a conditional design study with no new observations or planet detection. It uses two local neighborhoods, inherited timing errors and shape information, fixed stellar and RV scenario values, and no visibility constraints or RV likelihood. The scores are not calibrated detection significance levels.

display.caption: Timing differences, local orbit-refit separation scores, and nonlinear injection tests for two published models. No visibility constraints are applied.
